CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain and swelling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained an injury to his left ankle yesterday while on a walk with his wife. He stepped off a curb and landed on his ankle incorrectly. He denies hearing or feeling a pop at the time of injury but reports the ankle felt extended and stretched. He was able to walk back to the house with difficulty and pain, primarily on the lateral aspect of the ankle. Pain has been present for a couple of days since the incident. He rates his pain as 8/10 without medication, which improves to approximately 7/10 with ibuprofen or acetaminophen. He has been managing the injury at home with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing restriction.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies significant prior ankle injuries. Vitals noted to be stable with slight elevation attributed to pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history provided.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, as needed for pain)

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. He and his wife take regular walks for exercise and recreation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Stable with mild elevation due to pain. Left ankle exam reveals ecchymosis and swelling over the lateral malleolus with edema. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with soft tissue swelling. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot. Neurovascular exam: Capillary refill brisk (less than 3 seconds). Strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally. Motor and sensory function intact and symmetric bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. Patient to continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, compression, elevation). Prescribed air cast for ankle stabilization. Crutches prescribed with instruction to stay off affected leg but begin walking as tolerated. Continue NSAIDs to reduce pain and swelling. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient instructed to return if pain significantly worsens or for any concerns prior to follow-up visit.
